children: Unlike in recent years, the British economy has sustained its early-year momentum into the second half of 2026, Oxford Economics' Andrew Goodwin says in a note. "This likely reflects a combination of genuine strength due to structural change because of IT-related investment, but also noisy data," he says. Rapid increases in AI usage mean recent IT strength will likely endure, though strong pickup in professional services output in the last six months is harder to explain. Any resilience will come under pressure over the next few quarters, particularly given most of the impact of the Middle East war is still to come. Financial conditions have worsened, and fiscal policy is being tightened, he adds. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)
